ko.title: 4.2%의 환상: 안정적인 실업률이 줄어드는 노동력을 감추고 있을 수 있는 이유

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 미국의

segments.src: unemployment rate has become the most reassuring number in the economy — and possibly the most misleading one.
segments.tr: 실업률은 경제에서 가장 안심을 주는 수치이자, 어쩌면 가장 오해를 불러일으키는 수치가 되었습니다.

segments.src: It has been parked at 4.2%, a level that in most decades would describe a labor market in good health.
segments.tr: 이 수치는 4.2%에 머물러 있으며, 이는 대부분의 수십 년 동안 건전한 상태의 노동 시장을 나타내는 수준입니다.

segments.src: But the June employment report told a different story underneath the headline.
segments.tr: 그러나 6월 고용 보고서는 헤드라인 이면에서 다른 이야기를 전했습니다.

segments.src: Payrolls grew by roughly 57,000 jobs, well short of the 115,000 economists had penciled in.
segments.tr: 급여 고용은 약 57,000개 증가하여, 경제학자들이 예상했던 115,000개에 한참 못 미쳤습니다.

segments.src: Revisions took another 74,000 jobs out of the April and May figures combined.
segments.tr: 수정치로 인해 4월과 5월 수치에서 합산 74,000개의 일자리가 추가로 사라졌습니다.

segments.src: And the labor force participation rate slipped to 61.5% — the lowest reading since March 2021, when the economy was still climbing out of the pandemic hole.
segments.tr: 그리고 경제활동참가율은 61.5%로 떨어졌으며, 이는 경제가 여전히 팬데믹의 늪에서 벗어나고 있던 2021년 3월 이후 가장 낮은 수치입니다.

segments.src: Those three facts sit uneasily together.
segments.tr: 이 세 가지 사실은 함께 편안하게 자리 잡지 못합니다.

segments.src: Hiring slowed, past months were marked down, and yet the unemployment rate did not move.
segments.tr: 고용은 둔화되었고, 지난달 수치는 하향 조정되었음에도 실업률은 움직이지 않았습니다.

segments.src: Understanding why requires looking at how the rate is built.
segments.tr: 그 이유를 이해하려면 실업률이 어떻게 산출되는지 살펴봐야 합니다.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## 헤드라인을 보기 좋게 포장하는 산술

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: 실업률은 인원수가 아니라 분수입니다.

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: 분자는 일자리가 없으면서 *적극적으로* 구직 중인 사람들의 수입니다.

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: 분모는 노동력으로, 일하는 모든 사람과 적극적으로 구직 중인 모든 사람을 합친 것입니다.

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: 결정적으로, 구직을 중단하면 방정식의 양쪽 모두에서 벗어나게 됩니다.

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: 당신은 실업자로 집계되지 않습니다.

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: 아예 집계되지 않는 것입니다.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: 단순화된 예시를 보면 메커니즘이 명확해집니다.

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: 1,000명의 노동력 중 42명이 실업 상태라고 상상해 보십시오.

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
segments.tr: 실업률은 4.2%입니다.

segments.src: Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: 이제 그 42명 중 10명이 구직을 포기한다고 가정해 봅시다. 조기 은퇴를 하거나, 학업으로 복귀하거나, 전업 육아를 맡거나, 단순히 일자리가 없다고 결론을 내리는 것입니다.

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: 다음 달에는 990명의 노동력 중 32명이 실업 상태가 됩니다.

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: 실업률은 대략 3.2%로 떨어집니다.

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: 아무도 일자리를 찾지 못했습니다.

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: 수치는 어쨌든 개선되었습니다.

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: 이는 통계의 결함이라기보다는 그것이 측정하도록 설계된 것의 한계에 가깝습니다.

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: 실업률은 좁은 질문에 답합니다. 일을 원하고 구직 중인 사람들 중에서 일자리를 찾지 못한 사람의 비율은 얼마인가?

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: 이 수치는 애초에 대부분의 사람들이 실제로 관심을 갖는 더 넓은 질문, 즉 지금 당장 일자리를 구하고 유지하기가 얼마나 쉬운가에 답하기 위한 것이 아니었습니다.

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## 경제활동참가율이 더해주는 것

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: 거기서 경제활동참가율이 등장합니다.

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: 61.5%라는 수치는 근로 연령에 해당하는 미국인 100명 중 62명 미만이 취업 상태이거나 구직 활동을 하고 있음을 의미합니다.

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: 배경을 설명하자면, 경제활동참가율은 2020년 초 팬데믹 직전에는 약 63.3%였으며, 밀레니엄 전환기에는 약 67%로 정점을 찍었습니다.

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: 그 이후의 오랜 하락세는 전체적으로 미스터리가 아닙니다. 인구가 고령화되고 있으며 은퇴하는 베이비부머들이 매년 기계적으로 수치를 끌어내리고 있습니다.

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: 현재 상황을 읽는 데 중요한 것은 하락의 *속도*와 떠나는 사람들의 구성입니다.

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: 다음 사이에는 의미 있는 차이가 있습니다:

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **구조적 이탈.** 예정된 은퇴, 학업 복귀, 또는 보육 및 노인 돌봄 비용이 일자리가 주는 급여를 초과하여 떠나는 사람들. 감소한 이민 유입으로 인한 느린 노동력 성장도 여기에 나타납니다. 이는 시간이 지남에 따라 경제의 잠재력을 축소하지만 현재의 약세를 나타내는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **구직 단념.** 일자리를 원하고, 구직 활동을 했으나 찾지 못해 멈춘 사람들. 이는 변장한 경기 순환적 약세입니다. 노동 시장이 악화되는 바로 그 시점에 실업률이 더 좋아 보이게 만듭니다.

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: 단 한 번의 월간 보고서로는 이 둘을 깔끔하게 분리할 수 없습니다.

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: 도움이 되는 데이터는 헤드라인 아래에 묻혀 있습니다. 핵심 연령층 경제활동참가율(25~54세, 대부분의 은퇴 효과를 제외함), 노동시장 주변참가자 수, 그리고 구직 단념자와 풀타임 근무를 원하지만 파트타임에 머문 사람들을 포함하는 광의의 U-6 지표가 그것입니다.

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: 핵심 연령층 참여가 하락하고 있다면, 은퇴 인구통계는 그 설명이 될 수 없습니다.

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## 수정치가 평소보다 더 중요한 이유

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: 4월과 5월에서 지워진 74,000개의 일자리는 대충 넘어가기 쉽습니다.

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: 그렇게 해서는 안 됩니다.

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: 급여 고용 수치는 첫 번째 추정치가 발표된 후 두 달 동안 계속 응답을 수집하는 고용주 설문조사에서 나옵니다.

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: 초기 수치는 응답하기에는 너무 신생이거나 최근에 폐업한 기업들에 의해 창출되고 사라진 일자리를 추정하는 통계 모델에 의존합니다.

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: 경제 국면이 전환될 때 그 모델은 느린 경향이 있습니다. 경기가 식을 때 고용 창출을 과대평가하고 경기가 가열될 때 과소평가할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: 설문조사 응답률도 수년에 걸쳐 낮아졌으며, 이는 단일 월의 오차 범위를 넓힙니다.

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: 실용적인 결론은 연속적인 하향 수정 자체가 정보라는 점입니다.

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: 이는 노동 시장의 초안이 최종 버전보다 체계적으로 더 낙관적이었음을 시사하며, 이는 7월의 최초 발표치도 동일한 할인율을 적용하여 읽어야 함을 의미합니다.

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## 상황이 괜찮다는 주장

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: 공정성상 장부의 다른 측면도 보아야 하며, 그곳이 비어 있는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: 해고는 역사적으로 낮은 수준을 유지했습니다.

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: 실업보험 주간 청구 건수는 이용 가능한 가장 고주파의 고용 신호인데, 진정한 경기 침체와 일치할 방식으로 급등하지 않았습니다.

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: 2021년 이후 인력 충원에 어려움을 겪었던 많은 고용주들은 감원을 꺼리는 것으로 보이며, 이는 흔히 노동 비축(labor hoarding)이라고 불리는 행동입니다.

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: 그것이 묘사하는 것은 저채용, 저해고 시장입니다.

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: 일자리가 있다면 비교적 안전합니다.

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: 일자리를 찾고 있다면, 즉 신규 졸업자, 휴식 후 재진입자, 산업을 전환하려는 모든 사람에게는 경험이 4.2% 헤드라인이 암시하는 것보다 훨씬 더 어렵습니다.

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: 두 가지 모두 동시에 사실일 수 있으며, 그들 사이의 괴리가 바로 종합 수치가 가리는 것입니다.

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: 또한 실업률과 경제활동참가율이 두 가지 다른 설문조사에서 나온다는 점도 주목할 가치가 있습니다.

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: 실업률과 참여율은 가구 대상 설문조사에서 오고, 급여 고용 수는 고용주 대상 설문조사에서 옵니다.

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: 이 둘은 순전히 통계적 이유로 매월 정기적으로 일치하지 않으며, 어느 쪽도 그 자체로 결정적이진 않습니다.

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## 금요일에 확인할 가치가 있는 세 가지

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: 7월 보고서는 금요일에 발표되며 어떤 이야기가 맞는지 직접 테스트할 기회를 제공합니다.

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | 살펴볼 항목 | 중요한 이유 |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | 핵심 연령층(25~54세) 참여 | 안정적인 수치와 함께 상승한다면 시장이 실제로 노동자를 흡수하고 있음을 의미합니다. 하락한다면 채용이 아니라 이탈로 인해 수치가 지탱되고 있음을 의미합니다. |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | 5월과 5월의 수정치 | 4개월 연속 하향 조정은 둔화를 노이즈가 아닌 추세처럼 보이게 만들 것입니다. |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | U-6 실업률 대 헤드라인 실업률 | 벌어지는 격차는 메인 수치가 포착하지 못하는 구직 단념자와 비자발적 파트타임 고용을 가리킵니다. |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: 고용이 부진하고 *참여율이* 다시 하락하며 *실업률이* 4.2% 근처를 유지한다면, 헤드라인은 줄어드는 분모에 의해 포장되고 있는 것입니다.

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: 고용이 실망스러운 가운데 참여율이 반등하고 실업률이 상승한다면, 이는 틀림없이 더 건강한 신호입니다. 사람들이 포기하기보다는 구직으로 돌아오고 있음을 의미하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 결론

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: 안정적인 실업률이 안정적인 노동 시장과 같은 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: 구직자로 집계되는 사람들의 풀이 계속 줄어들 때, 구직자들의 여건이 악화되는 동안에도 실업률은 안정적으로 유지되거나 심지어 개선될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: 이 중 어느 것도 4.2%를 조작된 수치로 만들지 않습니다.

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: 그것은 불완전하게 만듭니다.

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: 이 숫자는 그것이 만들어진 대로 작동하고 있을 뿐이며, 대부분의 사람들이 그것에 묻고 있는 질문에 답하도록 만들어지지 않았을 뿐입니다.

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.

zh.title: 4.2%的错觉：为什么稳定的失业率可能掩盖了萎缩的劳动力队伍

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 美国

segments.src: unemployment rate has become the most reassuring number in the economy — and possibly the most misleading one.
segments.tr: 失业率已经成为经济中最让人安心的数字——也可能是最具误导性的数字。

segments.src: It has been parked at 4.2%, a level that in most decades would describe a labor market in good health.
segments.tr: 它一直停留在4.2%，在大多数十年里，这个水平意味着健康的劳动力市场。

segments.src: But the June employment report told a different story underneath the headline.
segments.tr: 但6月的就业报告在头条数据下呈现了截然不同的情况。

segments.src: Payrolls grew by roughly 57,000 jobs, well short of the 115,000 economists had penciled in.
segments.tr: 非农就业人数增加了约5.7万人，远低于经济学家预期的11.5万人。

segments.src: Revisions took another 74,000 jobs out of the April and May figures combined.
segments.tr: 修正数据使4月和5月的总数据减少了7.4万个工作岗位。

segments.src: And the labor force participation rate slipped to 61.5% — the lowest reading since March 2021, when the economy was still climbing out of the pandemic hole.
segments.tr: 劳动力参与率下滑至61.5%——创下2021年3月以来的最低水平，当时经济仍在努力摆脱疫情低谷。

segments.src: Those three facts sit uneasily together.
segments.tr: 这三个事实放在一起并不让人安心。

segments.src: Hiring slowed, past months were marked down, and yet the unemployment rate did not move.
segments.tr: 招聘放缓，前几个月数据被下调，然而失业率却没有动。

segments.src: Understanding why requires looking at how the rate is built.
segments.tr: 理解其中的原因需要审视失业率是如何计算出来的。

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## 装饰头条的算术

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: 失业率是一个分数，而不是人数统计。

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: 分子是没有工作*且*积极寻找工作的人数。

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: 分母是劳动力：所有工作的人加上所有积极寻找工作的人。

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: 关键在于，如果你停止寻找，你就会离开等式的两侧。

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: 你不会被算作失业。

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: 你根本不会被统计在内。

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: 一个简化的例子让其机制显而易见。

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: 想象一个由1,000人组成的劳动力队伍，其中42人失业。

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
segments.tr: 失业率为4.2%。

segments.src: Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: 现在假设这42人中有10人放弃了搜寻——他们提前退休、重返校园、承担全职照顾家人的工作，或者干脆认为外面什么也没有。

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: 下一个月，在990人的劳动力队伍中有32人失业。

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: 失业率降至约3.2%。

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: 没有人找到工作。

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: 但数字无论如何都变好了。

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: 这与其说是统计数据的缺陷，不如说是它被设计用来测量的极限。

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: 失业率回答了一个狭隘的问题：在想要工作并正在寻找工作的人中，有多少比例找不到工作？

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: 它从来不是为了回答大多数人真正关心的更广泛问题——现在找工作和保住工作有多容易？

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## 参与率补充了什么

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: 这就是参与率发挥作用的地方。

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: 在61.5%的水平下，它表明每100名适龄美国人中，不到62人处于就业状态或正在寻找工作。

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: 作为背景，在2020年初疫情爆发前夕，参与率大约在63.3%，并在千禧年之交达到约67%的峰值。

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: 从那以后漫长的下降在整体上并不神秘——人口在老龄化，退休的婴儿潮一代每年都在机械性地把数字拉低。

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: 对于解读当下至关重要的是下降的*速度*以及离开者的构成。

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: 以下两者之间存在重大区别：

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **结构性退出。** 按计划退休、重返校园，或者因为育儿和长者护理成本超过工作薪酬而离开的人。移民流入减少导致的劳动力增长放缓也体现在这里。这随着时间的推移缩小了经济的潜力，但并不预示着当前的疲软。

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **沮丧放弃。** 想要工作、寻找过但什么也没找到并停止了的人。这是伪装起来的周期性疲软——它恰好在劳动力市场恶化时让失业率看起来更好。

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: 单月的报告无法干净利落地将两者分开。

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: 有帮助的数据隐藏在头条之下：黄金年龄参与率（25-54岁，剔除了大部分退休影响）、与劳动力队伍边缘挂钩的人数，以及更广泛的U-6指标，其中包括沮丧的工人和想要全职工作却被困在兼职工作中的人。

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: 如果黄金年龄参与率在下滑，退休人口统计就不是解释。

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## 为什么修正数据比平时更重要

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: 从4月和5月数据中抹去的7.4万个工作岗位很容易被忽略。

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: 它们不应该被忽略。

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: 非农就业数据来自对雇主的调查，该调查在首次估计发布后还会继续收集两个月的回复。

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: 早期数字依赖于一个统计模型，该模型估计由太新或最近倒闭而无法回复的企业创造和失去的工作岗位。

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: 当经济转折时，该模型往往很慢——它可能在周期冷却时高估就业创造，在周期升温时低估就业创造。

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: 多年来，调查回复率也有所下降，这扩大了任何单月数据的误差范围。

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: 实际的启示是，连续向下修正本身就是一种信息。

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: 它表明劳动力市场的初稿比最终版本系统性地更为乐观——这意味着7月的初值也应在应用相同折扣的情况下进行解读。

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## 认为一切正常的观点

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: 公平要求看看账本的另一面，它并不是空的。

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: 裁员一直保持在历史低位。

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: 失业保险周申请人数——这是可获得的最高频率的劳动力信号——并没有以符合真正经济衰退的方式飙升。

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: 许多在2021年后难以招到人的雇主似乎不愿裁员，这种行为通常被称为劳动力囤积（labor hoarding）。

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: 这描述的是一个低招聘、低解雇的市场。

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: 如果你有一份工作，它是相当安全的。

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: 如果你正在找工作——新毕业生、休息后重新进入职场的人、任何试图转换行业的人——其体验要比4.2%的头条数据所暗示的困难得多。

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: 这两点可以同时成立，它们之间的分歧正是总体失业率所掩盖的。

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: 同样值得注意的是，失业率和参与率来自两个不同的调查。

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: 失业率和参与率来自对家庭的调查；就业人数来自对雇主的调查。

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: 出于纯粹的统计原因，这两者经常在按月对比时出现分歧，单凭任何一个都不能算作决定性的。

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## 周五值得检查的三件事

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: 7月报告将于周五发布，并为哪种说法是正确的提供直接检验。

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | 查看内容 | 为什么重要 |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | 黄金年龄（25-54岁）参与率 | 与稳定失业率一起上升意味着市场正在真正吸收工人。下降意味着失业率是由退出而不是招聘来支撑的。 |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | 对5月和6月的修正 | 连续第四个月向下修正将使放缓看起来像是一种趋势，而不是噪音。 |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | U-6失业率与头条失业率的对比 | 不断扩大的差距指向主要失业率没有捕捉到的沮丧工人和非自愿兼职就业。 |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: 如果就业数据疲软*且*参与率再次下降*且*失业率维持在4.2%附近，那么头条数据就被缩小的分母美化了。

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: 如果就业数据令人失望，而参与率上升且失业率上升，这可以说是一个更健康的信号——这意味着人们正在回归搜寻而不是放弃它。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 底线

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: 稳定的失业率不等于稳定的劳动力市场。

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: 当被算作寻找工作的人数不断萎缩时，在求职者条件恶化的同时，失业率可以保持稳定，甚至有所改善。

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: 这并没有把4.2%变成虚构。

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: 它让它变得不完整。

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: 这个数字正在做它被建造来做的事情——它只是没有被建造成来回答大多数人向它提出的问题。

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: 对于任何追踪经济的人来说，有用的习惯是停止孤立地阅读头条失业率，而是开始把它当作三行故事中的一行来读：增加了多少工作岗位，前几个月静悄悄地收回了多少，以及到底还有多少人在统计数字中。

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## वह अंकगणित जो मुख्य सुर्खियों को चापलूसी देता है

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: बेरोजगारी दर एक भिन्न (fraction) है, न कि सिरों की गिनती (headcount)।

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: अंश (numerator) उन लोगों की संख्या है जो काम से बाहर हैं *और* सक्रिय रूप से तलाश कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: हर (denominator) श्रम बल है: काम करने वाले सभी लोग प्लस सक्रिय रूप से तलाश करने वाले सभी लोग।

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि यदि आप तलाश करना बंद कर देते हैं, तो आप समीकरण के दोनों पक्षों को छोड़ देते हैं।

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: आपको बेरोजगार नहीं गिना जाता है।

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: आपको बिल्कुल भी नहीं गिना जाता है।

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: एक सरलीकृत उदाहरण यांत्रिकी को स्पष्ट करता है।

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: 1,000 लोगों के श्रम बल की कल्पना करें जिसमें 42 बेरोजगार हैं।

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: अब मान लीजिए कि उन 42 में से 10 अपनी तलाश छोड़ देते हैं — वे जल्दी सेवानिवृत्त हो जाते हैं, स्कूल वापस जाते हैं, पूर्णकालिक देखभाल संभालते हैं, या बस यह निष्कर्ष निकालते हैं कि बाहर कुछ भी नहीं है।

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: अगले महीने 990 के श्रम बल में 32 बेरोजगार हैं।

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: दर गिरकर लगभग 3.2% हो जाती है।

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: किसी को नौकरी नहीं मिली।

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: संख्या वैसे भी सुधर गई।

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: यह आँकड़े में कोई दोष उतना नहीं है जितना कि यह मापने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया था उसकी एक सीमा है।

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: बेरोजगारी दर एक संकीर्ण प्रश्न का उत्तर देती है: काम चाहने वाले और इसके लिए तलाश करने वाले लोगों में से, कौन सा हिस्सा इसे नहीं पा सकता है?

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: यह कभी भी उस व्यापक प्रश्न का उत्तर देने के लिए नहीं था जिसकी अधिकांश लोग वास्तव में परवाह करते हैं — अभी नौकरी पाना और बनाए रखना कितना आसान है?

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## भागीदारी दर क्या जोड़ती है

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: यही वह जगह है जहाँ भागीदारी दर आती है।

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: 61.5% पर, यह कहती है कि कामकाजी उम्र के हर 100 अमेरिकियों में से 62 से कम या तो कार्यरत हैं या नौकरी की तलाश कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: संदर्भ के लिए, महामारी से ठीक पहले 2020 की शुरुआत में भागीदारी लगभग 63.3% थी, और सहस्राब्दी की शुरुआत में लगभग 67% पर चरम पर थी।

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: तब से लंबी गिरावट कुल मिलाकर रहस्यमय नहीं है — आबादी बूढ़ी हो रही है, और सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले बेबी बूमर्स हर साल यंत्रवत् रूप से संख्या को नीचे खींचते हैं।

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: वर्तमान क्षण को पढ़ने के लिए जो मायने रखता है वह है गिरावट की *गति* और छोड़ने वालों की संरचना।

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: इसके बीच एक सार्थक अंतर है:

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **संरचनात्मक निकास।** निर्धारित समय पर सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले लोग, स्कूल लौट रहे हैं, या इसलिए छोड़ रहे हैं क्योंकि चाइल्डकैअर और एल्डरकेअर लागत नौकरी के वेतन से अधिक है। कम आप्रवासन प्रवाह से धीमी श्रम-बल वृद्धि भी यहाँ दिखाई देती है। यह समय के साथ अर्थव्यवस्था की क्षमता को सिकोड़ती है लेकिन वर्तमान कमजोरी का संकेत नहीं देती है।

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **निराशा।** वे लोग जो नौकरी चाहते थे, तलाश की, कुछ नहीं मिला, और रुक गए। यह एक छद्म रूप में चक्रीय कमजोरी है — यह बेरोजगारी दर को ठीक तब बेहतर बनाती है जब श्रम बाजार खराब हो रहा है।

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: एक अकेली मासिक रिपोर्ट दोनों को स्पष्ट रूप से अलग नहीं कर सकती है।

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: जो डेटा मदद करता है वह सुर्खियों के नीचे दफनाया गया है: प्रधान-आयु भागीदारी दर (आयु 25-54, जो अधिकांश सेवानिवृत्ति प्रभावों को हटा देती है), श्रम बल से मामूली रूप से जुड़े लोगों की गिनती, और व्यापक U-6 उपाय, जिसमें निराश श्रमिक और अंशकालिक नौकरियों में फंसे लोग शामिल हैं जो पूर्णकालिक घंटे चाहते हैं।

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: यदि प्रधान-आयु भागीदारी फिसल रही है, तो सेवानिवृत्ति जनसांख्यिकी स्पष्टीकरण नहीं है।

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## संशोधन सामान्य से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण क्यों हैं

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: अप्रैल और मई से मिटाए गए 74,000 नौकरियों को पार करना आसान है।

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: उन्हें नहीं होना चाहिए।

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: पेरोल के आंकड़े नियोजकों के एक सर्वेक्षण से आते हैं जो पहला अनुमान प्रकाशित होने के बाद दो महीने तक प्रतिक्रियाएं एकत्र करना जारी रखता है।

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: शुरुआती संख्याएं एक सांख्यिकीय मॉडल पर झुकती हैं जो प्रतिक्रिया देने के लिए बहुत नए या हाल ही में बंद व्यवसायों द्वारा बनाई गई और खोई हुई नौकरियों का अनुमान लगाती है।

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: जब अर्थव्यवस्था बदलती है, तो वह मॉडल धीमा होता है — यह चक्र ठंडा होने पर नौकरी के सृजन को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर पेश कर सकता है और चक्र गर्म होने पर इसे कम आंक सकता है।

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: सर्वेक्षण प्रतिक्रिया दरें भी वर्षों में नीचे आ गई हैं, जो किसी भी एक महीने पर त्रुटि के मार्जिन को चौड़ा करती हैं।

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: व्यावहारिक निष्कर्ष यह है कि लगातार नीचे की ओर संशोधनों की एक श्रृंखला अपने आप में जानकारी है।

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: यह सुझाव देता है कि श्रम बाजार का पहला मसौदा अंतिम संस्करण की तुलना में व्यवस्थित रूप से अधिक गुलाबी रहा है — जिसका अर्थ है कि जुलाई के लिए प्रारंभिक प्रिंट को उसी छूट को लागू करके पढ़ा जाना चाहिए।

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## यह मामला कि चीजें ठीक हैं

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: निष्पक्षता के लिए बहीखाता के दूसरी तरफ की आवश्यकता होती है, और यह खाली नहीं है।

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: छंटनी ऐतिहासिक रूप से कम बनी हुई है।

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: बेरोजगारी बीमा के लिए साप्ताहिक दावे — उपलब्ध सबसे अधिक आवृत्ति वाला श्रम संकेत — उस तरह से नहीं बढ़े हैं जो एक वास्तविक मंदी के अनुरूप होगा।

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: 2021 के बाद कर्मचारियों को रखने के लिए संघर्ष करने वाले कई नियोक्ता कटौती करने में संकोच करते दिखाई देते हैं, एक ऐसा व्यवहार जिसे अक्सर श्रम होर्डिंग कहा जाता है।

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: यह जो वर्णन करता है वह कम-भर्ती, कम-आग का बाजार है।

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: यदि आपके پاس नौकरी है, तो यह काफी सुरक्षित है।

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: यदि आप एक की तलाश कर रहे हैं — एक नया स्नातक, एक ब्रेक के बाद फिर से प्रवेश करने वाला कोई व्यक्ति, उद्योगों को बदलने की कोशिश कर रहा कोई भी व्यक्ति — अनुभव 4.2% सुर्खियों के निहितार्थ की तुलना में काफी कठिन है।

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: दोनों चीजें एक साथ सच हो सकती हैं, और उनके बीच का विचलन वही है जो कुल दर अस्पष्ट करती है।

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: यह भी ध्यान देने योग्य है कि बेरोजगारी दर और भागीदारी दर दो अलग-अलग सर्वेक्षणों से आती हैं।

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: दर और भागीदारी घरों के सर्वेक्षण से आती है; पेरोल गिनती नियोजकों के सर्वेक्षण से आती है।

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: दोनों नियमित रूप से विशुद्ध रूप से सांख्यिकीय कारणों से महीने-दर-महीने असहमत होते हैं, और न ही अपने दम पर निश्चित है।

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## शुक्रवार को जाँचने लायक तीन बातें

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: जुलाई की रिपोर्ट शुक्रवार को आती है और इस बात का सीधा परीक्षण प्रदान करती है कि कौन सी कहानी सही है।

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | क्या देखें | यह क्यों महत्वपूर्ण है |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | प्रधान-आयु (25–54) भागीदारी | एक स्थिर दर के साथ बढ़ना मतलब बाजार वास्तव में श्रमिकों को अवशोषित कर रहा है। गिरना मतलब दर निकास द्वारा समर्थित हो रही है, न कि काम पर रखने से। |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | मई और जून में संशोधन | नीचे के निशान का लगातार चौथा महीना मंदी को शोर के बजाय एक प्रवृत्ति की तरह दिखाएगा। |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | U-6 दर बनाम सुर्खियाँ | एक चौड़ा होता अंतर निराश श्रमिकों और अनैच्छिक अंशकालिक रोजगार की ओर इशारा करता है जिसे मुख्य दर कैप्चर नहीं करती है। |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: यदि पेरोल नरम आते हैं *और* भागीदारी फिर से गिरती है *और* दर 4.2% के करीब रखती है, तो सुर्खियों में सिकुड़ते हर (denominator) द्वारा चापलूसी की जा रही है।

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: यदि पेरोल निराशाजनक हैं जबकि भागीदारी टिक जाती है और दर बढ़ती है, तो यह यकीनन एक स्वस्थ संकेत है — इसका मतलब है कि लोग इसे छोड़ने के बजाय तलाश में लौट रहे हैं।

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## निचला रेखा

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: एक स्थिर बेरोजगारी दर एक स्थिर श्रम बाजार के समान नहीं है।

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: जब काम की तलाश करने वाले गिने जाने वाले लोगों का पूल सिकुड़ता रहता है, तो दर स्थिर रह सकती है, या यहाँ तक कि सुधार भी सकती है, जबकि नौकरी चाहने वालों के लिए स्थिति खराब होती है।

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: इनमें से कोई भी 4.2% को मनगढ़ंत नहीं बनाता है।

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: यह इसे अधूरा बनाता है।

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.

es.title: La ilusión del 4.2%: Por qué una tasa de desempleo estable puede estar ocultando una fuerza laboral en contracción

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: La tasa de desempleo de

segments.src: unemployment rate has become the most reassuring number in the economy — and possibly the most misleading one.
segments.tr: EE. UU. se ha convertido en el número más tranquilizador de la economía — y posiblemente en el más engañoso.

segments.src: It has been parked at 4.2%, a level that in most decades would describe a labor market in good health.
segments.tr: Se ha mantenido en el 4.2%, un nivel que en la mayoría de las décadas describiría un mercado laboral en buena salud.

segments.src: But the June employment report told a different story underneath the headline.
segments.tr: Pero el informe de empleo de junio contó una historia diferente bajo el titular.

segments.src: Payrolls grew by roughly 57,000 jobs, well short of the 115,000 economists had penciled in.
segments.tr: Las nóminas crecieron en aproximadamente 57,000 empleos, muy por debajo de los 115,000 que los economistas habían previsto.

segments.src: Revisions took another 74,000 jobs out of the April and May figures combined.
segments.tr: Las revisiones restaron otros 74,000 empleos de las cifras combinadas de abril y mayo.

segments.src: And the labor force participation rate slipped to 61.5% — the lowest reading since March 2021, when the economy was still climbing out of the pandemic hole.
segments.tr: Y la tasa de participación en la fuerza laboral cayó al 61.5%, la lectura más baja desde marzo de 2021, cuando la economía aún salía del bache de la pandemia.

segments.src: Those three facts sit uneasily together.
segments.tr: Esos tres datos encajan incómodamente.

segments.src: Hiring slowed, past months were marked down, and yet the unemployment rate did not move.
segments.tr: La contratación se desaceleró, los meses pasados se redujeron a la baja y, sin embargo, la tasa de desempleo no se movió.

segments.src: Understanding why requires looking at how the rate is built.
segments.tr: Comprender por qué requiere observar cómo se construye la tasa.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## La aritmética que favorece al titular

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: La tasa de desempleo es una fracción, no un recuento de personas.

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: El numerador es el número de personas que están sin trabajo *y* buscando activamente.

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: El denominador es la fuerza laboral: todos los que trabajan más todos los que buscan activamente.

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: De manera crucial, si dejas de buscar, abandonas ambos lados de la ecuación.

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: No se te cuenta como desempleado.

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: No se te cuenta en absoluto.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: Un ejemplo simplificado hace que la mecánica sea obvia.

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: Imagina una fuerza laboral de 1,000 personas con 42 desempleados.

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
segments.tr: La tasa es del 4.2%.

segments.src: Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: Ahora supongamos que 10 de esos 42 abandonan su búsqueda: se jubilan anticipadamente, vuelven a estudiar, asumen el cuidado de tiempo completo o simplemente concluyen que no hay nada ahí fuera.

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: El mes siguiente hay 32 desempleados en una fuerza laboral de 990.

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: La tasa cae aproximadamente al 3.2%.

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: Nadie encontró trabajo.

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: El número mejoró de todos modos.

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: Esto no es tanto un fallo en la estadística como un límite en lo que fue diseñada para medir.

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: La tasa de desempleo responde a una pregunta estrecha: entre las personas que quieren trabajar y lo buscan, ¿qué proporción no puede encontrarlo?

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: Nunca tuvo la intención de responder a la pregunta más amplia que a la mayoría de la gente realmente le importa: ¿qué tan fácil es conseguir y mantener un trabajo en este momento?

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## Lo que aporta la tasa de participación

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: Aquí es donde entra la tasa de participación.

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: Con un 61.5%, indica que menos de 62 de cada 100 estadounidenses en edad de trabajar están empleados o buscando empleo.

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: Como contexto, la participación se situaba en aproximadamente el 63.3% justo antes de la pandemia a principios de 2020, y alcanzó un máximo de alrededor del 67% en el cambio de milenio.

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: El largo declive desde entonces no es misterioso en conjunto: la población está envejeciendo y los *baby boomers* que se jubilan tiran mecánicamente de la cifra hacia abajo cada año.

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: Lo que importa para leer el momento actual es el *ritmo* de la caída y la composición de quiénes se van.

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: Existe una diferencia significativa entre:

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **Salida estructural.** Personas que se jubilan según lo programado, regresan a estudiar o se van porque los costos de cuidado infantil y de ancianos superan lo que paga un empleo. El menor crecimiento de la fuerza laboral debido a flujos de inmigración reducidos también aparece aquí. Esto reduce el potencial de la economía con el tiempo, pero no indica debilidad actual.

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **Desaliento.** Personas que quieren un trabajo, buscaron, no encontraron nada y se detuvieron. Esto es debilidad cíclica disfrazada: hace que la tasa de desempleo se vea mejor precisamente cuando el mercado laboral está empeorando.

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: Un solo informe mensual no puede separar claramente ambas cosas.

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: Los datos que ayudan están enterrados bajo el titular: la tasa de participación en edad principal (25–54 años, que elimina la mayoría de los efectos de jubilación), el recuento de personas marginalmente vinculadas a la fuerza laboral y la medida más amplia U-6, que incluye a los trabajadores desalentados y personas atrapadas en empleos a tiempo parcial que desean horas de tiempo completo.

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: Si la participación en la edad principal está cayendo, la demografía de la jubilación no es la explicación.

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## Por qué las revisiones importan más de lo habitual

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: Los 74,000 empleos borrados de abril y mayo son fáciles de pasar por alto.

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: No deberían serlo.

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: Las cifras de nóminas provienen de una encuesta a empleadores que sigue recopilando respuestas durante dos meses después de que se publica la primera estimación.

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: Los primeros números se apoyan en un modelo estadístico que estima los empleos creados y perdidos por empresas demasiado nuevas o cerradas recientemente para responder.

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: Cuando la economía cambia de rumbo, ese modelo tiende a ser lento: puede sobrestimar la creación de empleo a medida que el ciclo se enfría y subestimarla a medida que se calienta.

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: Las tasas de respuesta a las encuestas también han disminuido con los años, lo que amplía el margen de error en cualquier mes determinado.

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: La conclusión práctica es que una serie de revisiones a la baja consecutivas es información en sí misma.

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: Sugiere que el primer borrador del mercado laboral ha sido sistemáticamente más optimista que la versión final, lo que significa que la cifra inicial de julio debe leerse aplicando ese mismo descuento.

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## El argumento de que las cosas están bien

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: La equidad requiere el otro lado del balance, y no está vacío.

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: Los despidos se han mantenido históricamente bajos.

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: Las solicitudes semanales de seguro de desempleo — la señal laboral de mayor frecuencia disponible — no se han disparado de una manera que sea consistente con una recesión genuina.

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: Muchos empleadores que tuvieron dificultades para contratar después de 2021 parecen reacios a recortar, un comportamiento a menudo llamado acaparamiento de mano de obra.

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: Lo que esto describe es un mercado de baja contratación y baja rotación.

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: Si tienes un trabajo, es razonablemente seguro.

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: Si estás buscando uno — un recién graduado, alguien que reingresa tras una pausa, cualquiera que intente cambiar de industria — la experiencia es considerablemente más difícil de lo que implica un titular del 4.2%.

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: Ambas cosas pueden ser verdad al mismo tiempo, y la divergencia entre ellas es exactamente lo que la tasa agregada oscurece.

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: También vale la pena señalar que la tasa de desempleo y la tasa de participación provienen de dos encuestas diferentes.

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: La tasa y la participación provienen de una encuesta de hogares; el recuento de nóminas proviene de una encuesta de empleadores.

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: Las dos difieren regularmente mes a mes por razones puramente estadísticas, y ninguna es definitiva por sí sola.

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## Tres cosas que vale la pena comprobar el viernes

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: El informe de julio se publica el viernes y ofrece una prueba directa de qué historia es la correcta.

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | Qué observar | Por qué importa |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | Participación en edad principal (25–54) | Un aumento junto con una tasa estable significa que el mercado está absorbiendo genuinamente a los trabajadores. Una caída significa que la tasa se sostiene por salidas, no por contrataciones. |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | Revisiones a mayo y junio | Un cuarto mes consecutivo de marcas a la baja haría que la desaceleración pareciera una tendencia en lugar de ruido. |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | La tasa U-6 frente al titular | Una brecha que se amplía apunta a trabajadores desalentados y empleo involuntario a tiempo parcial que la tasa principal no capta. |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: Si las nóminas salen débiles *y* la participación cae nuevamente *y* la tasa se mantiene cerca del 4.2%, el titular está siendo favorecido por un denominador en contracción.

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: Si las nóminas decepcionan mientras la participación repunta y la tasa sube, eso es posiblemente una señal más saludable: significa que la gente está volviendo a la búsqueda en lugar de abandonarla.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## El resultado final

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: Una tasa de desempleo estable no es lo mismo que un mercado laboral estable.

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: Cuando el grupo de personas consideradas como buscadores de empleo sigue contrayéndose, la tasa puede mantenerse estable, o incluso mejorar, mientras las condiciones para quienes buscan empleo se deterioran.

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: Nada de esto hace que el 4.2% sea una fabricación.

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: Lo hace incompleto.

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: El número está haciendo lo que fue creado para hacer — simplemente no está diseñado para responder a la pregunta que la mayoría de la gente le hace.

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: Para cualquiera que siga la economía, el hábito útil es dejar de leer la tasa principal de forma aislada y empezar a leerla como una línea en una historia de tres líneas: cuántos empleos se agregaron, cuántos se retiraron silenciosamente de meses anteriores y cuántas personas siguen estando en el recuento.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.

segments.tr: في الشهر التالي يوجد 32 عاطلا في قوة عمل مكونة من 990.

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: ينخفض المعدل إلى ما يقريب من 3.2٪.

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: لم يجد أحد وظيفة.

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: تحسن الرقم على أي حال.

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: هذا ليس عيبا في الإحصاء بقدر ما هو حد لما صُمم لقياسه.

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: يجيب معدل البطالة على سؤال ضيق: بين الأشخاص الذين يريدون العمل ويبحثون عنه، ما هي النسبة التي لا تستطيع العثور عليه؟

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: لم يُقصد به أبدا الإجابة على السؤال الأوسع الذي تهتم به الغالبية العظمى من الناس في الواقع — ما مدى سهولة الحصول على وظيفة والاحتفاظ بها الآن؟

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## ما يضيفه معدل المشاركة

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: هنا يأتي دور معدل المشاركة.

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: عند 61.5٪، فإنه يشير إلى أن أقل من 62 من كل 100 أمريكي في سن العمل إما عاملين أو يبحثون عن عمل.

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: للسياق، كانت المشاركة عند نحو 63.3٪ قبيل الوباء في أوائل عام 2020، وبلغت ذروتها عند حوالي 67٪ مع مطلع الألفية.

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: الانهيار الطويل منذ ذلك الحين ليس غامضا في مجمله — السكان يتقدمون في السن، والمواليد القدامى المتقاعدون يسحبون الرقم نحو الانخفاض تلقائيا كل عام.

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: ما يهم لقراءة اللحظة الحالية هو *وتيرة* الانخفاض وتركيبة المغادرين.

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: هناك فرق ذو معنى بين:

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **الخروج الهيكلي.** الأشخاص الذين يتقاعدون في الموعد المحدد، أو يعودون إلى المدرسة، أو يغادرون لأن تكاليف رعاية الأطفال ورعاية المسنين تتجاوز ما تدفعه الوظيفة. يظهر هنا أيضاً نمو أبطأ للقوى العاملة ناتج عن انخفاض تدفقات الهجرة. هذا يقلص إمكانات الاقتصاد بمرور الوقت ولكنه لا يشير إلى ضعف حالي.

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **الإحباط.** الأشخاص الذين يريدون وظيفة، وبحثوا، ولم يجدوا شيئا، وتوقفوا. هذا ضعف دوري يرتدي قناعا — فهو يجعل معدل البطالة يبدو أفضل على وجه التحديد عندما تسوء سوق العمل.

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: تقرير شهري واحد لا يمكنه فصل الاثنين بشكل نظيف.

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: البيانات التي تساعد مدفونة تحت العنوان الرئيسي: معدل المشاركة في سن العمل الأساسي (25-54 عاما، والذي يستبعد معظم تأثيرات التقاعد)، وعددهم الأشخاص المرتبطون بشكل هامشي بالقوى العاملة، ومقياس U-6 الأوسع، والذي يتضمن العمال المحبطين والأشخاص العالقين في وظائف بدوام جزئي ويريدون ساعات بدوام كامل.

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: إذا كانت مشاركة سن العمل الأساسي في انخفاض، فالتركيبة السكانية للتقاعد ليست هي التفسير.

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## لماذا تهم المراجعات أكثر من المعتاد

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: الوظائف الـ 74,000 التي تم محوها من أبريل ومايو من السهل تجاوزها.

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: يجب ألا تكون كذلك.

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: تأتي أرقام الرواتب من مسح لأصحاب العمل يستمر في جمع الردود لمدة شهرين بعد نشر التقدير الأول.

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: تعتمد الأرقام المبكرة على نموذج إحصائي يقدر الوظائف التي أنشأتها وخسرتها الشركات التي تكون أحدث من أن تستجيب أو أغلقت مؤخرا.

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: عندما يتحول الاقتصاد، يميل هذا النموذج إلى أن يكون بطيئا — يمكن أن يبالغ في تقدير خلق الوظائف مع برودة الدورة ويهون منها مع سخونة الدورة.

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: كما تراجعت معدلات الاستجابة للمسح على مر السنين، مما يوسع هامش الخطأ في أي شهر منفرد.

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: الخلاصة العملية هي أن سلسلة من المراجعات المتتالية نحو الانخفاض هي بحد ذاتها معلومة.

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: وهذا يشير إلى أن المسودة الأولى لسوق العمل كانت أكثر تفاؤلاً بشكل منهجي من النسخة النهائية - مما يعني أن القراءة الأولية لشولي يجب أن تقرأ مع تطبيق نفس الخصم.

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## حجّة أن الأمور على ما يرام

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: تتطلب العدالة النظر إلى الجانب الآخر من السجل، وهو ليس فارغاً.

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: ظلّت عمليات تسريح العمال منخفضة تاريخياً.

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: لم ترتفع مطالبات التأمين الأسبوعية ضد البطالة - وهي إشارة العمل الأعلى تردداً المتاحة - بطريقة تتسق مع ركود حقيقي.

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: يبدو أن العديد من أصحاب العمل الذين عانوا لتوفير الموظفين بعد عام 2021 مترددون في التخفيض، وهو سلوك يسمى غالباً اكتناز العمالة.

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: ما يصفه ذلك هو سوق منخفض التوظيف منخفض التسريح.

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: إذا كان لديك وظيفة، فهي آمنة إلى حد معقول.

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: إذا كنت تبحث عن واحدة - خريج جديد، شخص يعود بعد استراحة، أي شخص يحاول تغيير الصناعة - تكون التجربة أصعب بكثير مما يعنيه العنوان الرئيسي لـ 4.2٪.

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: يمكن أن يكون الامرّان صحيحين في نفس الوقت، والتناقض بينهما هو بالضبط ما يخفيه المعدل الإجمالي.

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: تجدر الإشارة أيضاً إلى أن معدل البطالة ومعدل المشاركة يأتيان من مسحين مختلفين.

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: يأتي المعدل والمشاركة من مسح للأسر؛ بينما يأتي عد الرواتب من مسح لأصحاب العمل.

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: يتخالف الاثنان بانتظام شهراً بعد شهر لأسباب إحصائية بحتة، ولا يعتبر أي منهما نهائياً بمفرده.

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## ثلاثة أمور تستحق التحقق منها يوم الجمعة

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: يصل تقرير يوليو يوم الجمعة ويقدم اختباراً مباشراً لأي القصة صحيحة.

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | ما الذي يجب البحث عنه | لماذا هو مهم |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | مشاركة سن العمل الأساسي (25-54) | الارتفاع جنباً إلى جنب مع معدل مستقر يعني أن السوق يستوعب حقاً العمال. الانخفاض يعني أن المعدل مدعوم بالمغادرات، وليس التوظيف. |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | المراجعات لشهر مايو ويजून | شهر رابع على التوالي من العلامات نحو الانخفاض سيجعل التباطؤ يبدو وكأنه اتجاه بدلاً من ضوضاء. |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | معدل U-6 مقابل العنوان الرئيسي | الفجوة المتسعة تشير إلى عمال محبطين وتوظيف غير إرادي بدوام جزئي لا يلتقطه المعدل الرئيسي. |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: إذا جاءت الرواتب ضعيفة *وانخفضت* المشاركة مرة أخرى *وظل* المعدل قرب 4.2٪، فإن العنوان الرئيسي يتم تجميله بواسطة مقام يتقلص.

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: إذا خيبت الرواتب الآمال بينما ارتفعت المشاركة وارتفع المعدل، فهذه إشارة أكثر صحة يمكن القول - فهي تعني أن الناس يعودون إلى البحث بدلاً من التخلي عنه.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## الخلاصة النهائية

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: معدل البطالة المستقر ليس هو نفس سوق العمل المستقر.

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: عندما يستمر تجمع الأشخاص الذين يُحسبون كباحثين عن عمل في التقلص، يمكن أن يظل المعدل مستقراً، أو حتى يتحسن، بينما تتدهور الظروف للباحثين عن عمل.

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: لا شيء من هذا يجعل 4.2٪ تلفيقاً.

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: إنه يجعله غير مكتمل.

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: الرقم يقوم بما بُني للقيام به — إنه ببساطة غير مصمم للإجابة على السؤال الذي يطرحه عليه معظم الناس.

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: بالنسبة لأي شخص تتبع الاقتصاد، العادة المفيدة هي التوقف عن قراءة المعدل الرئيسي بمعزل عن غيره والبدء في قراءته كسطر واحد في قصة من ثلاثة أسطر: كم عدد الوظائف التي أضيفت، وكم عدد الوظائف التي سُحبت بهدوء من الشهور السابقة، وكم عدد الأشخاص الذين ما زالوا في العد على الإطلاق.

segments.tr: *يُقدم هذا المقال لأغراض معلوماتية عامة فقط ولا يشكل مشورة مالية أو استثمارية أو توظيفية.

segments.src: Employment figures cited are preliminary government estimates and are subject to revision.
segments.tr: أرقام التوظيف المذكورة هي تقديرات حكومية أولية وتخضع للمراجعة.

segments.src: Readers should consult official releases from the U.S.
segments.tr: يجب على القراء استشارة الإصدارات الرسمية من مكتب إحصاءات العمل الأمريكي
