fr.title: L'illusion des 4,2% : Pourquoi un taux de chômage stable peut masquer la contraction de la population active

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Le taux de chômage aux

segments.src: unemployment rate has become the most reassuring number in the economy — and possibly the most misleading one.
segments.tr: États-Unis est devenu le chiffre le plus rassurant de l'économie — et peut-être le plus trompeur.

segments.src: It has been parked at 4.2%, a level that in most decades would describe a labor market in good health.
segments.tr: Il est resté ancré à 4,2 %, un niveau qui, dans la plupart des décennies, décrirait un marché du travail en bonne santé.

segments.src: But the June employment report told a different story underneath the headline.
segments.tr: Mais le rapport sur l'emploi de juin a raconté une autre histoire sous le titre principal.

segments.src: Payrolls grew by roughly 57,000 jobs, well short of the 115,000 economists had penciled in.
segments.tr: Les créations d'emplois ont atteint environ 57 000, soit bien en deçà des 115 000 prévues par les économistes.

segments.src: Revisions took another 74,000 jobs out of the April and May figures combined.
segments.tr: Des révisions ont soustrait 74 000 emplois supplémentaires des chiffres combinés d'avril et de mai.

segments.src: And the labor force participation rate slipped to 61.5% — the lowest reading since March 2021, when the economy was still climbing out of the pandemic hole.
segments.tr: Et le taux d'activité a glissé à 61,5 %, soit le niveau le plus bas depuis mars 2021, alors que l'économie sortait encore du gouffre de la pandémie.

segments.src: Those three facts sit uneasily together.
segments.tr: Ces trois faits s'accordent mal.

segments.src: Hiring slowed, past months were marked down, and yet the unemployment rate did not move.
segments.tr: Les embauches ont ralenti, les mois précédents ont été révisés à la baisse, et pourtant le taux de chômage n'a pas bougé.

segments.src: Understanding why requires looking at how the rate is built.
segments.tr: Comprendre pourquoi exige d'examiner la construction de ce taux.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## L'arithmétique qui flatte le titre

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: Le taux de chômage est une fraction, non un décompte de personnes.

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: Le numérateur est le nombre de personnes sans emploi *et* activement à la recherche d'un travail.

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: Le dénominateur est la population active : toutes les personnes qui travaillent plus toutes celles qui cherchent activement.

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: De manière cruciale, si vous arrêtez de chercher, vous quittez les deux côtés de l'équation.

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: Vous n'êtes plus compté comme chômeur.

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: Vous n'êtes plus compté du tout.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: Un exemple simplifié rend la mécanique évidente.

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: Imaginez une population active de 1 000 personnes avec 42 chômeurs.

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
segments.tr: Le taux est de 4,2 %.

segments.src: Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: Supposons maintenant que 10 de ces 42 abandonnent leur recherche — ils prennent une retraite anticipée, retournent à l'école, prennent en charge des soins à temps plein ou concluent simplement qu'il n'y a rien.

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: Le mois suivant, il y a 32 chômeurs dans une population active de 990.

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: Le taux tombe à environ 3,2%.

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: Personne n'a trouvé de travail.

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: Le chiffre s'est amélioré malgré tout.

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: Ce n'est pas tant un défaut de la statistique qu'une limite de ce qu'elle a été conçue pour mesurer.

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: Le taux de chômage répond à une question étroite : parmi les personnes qui veulent travailler et le chercheur, quelle proportion ne peut pas en trouver ?

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: Il n'a jamais été censé répondre à la question plus large qui importe vraiment à la plupart des gens — est-il facile d'obtenir et de garder un emploi en ce moment ?

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## Ce qu'ajoute le taux d'activité

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: C'est là qu'intervient le taux d'activité.

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: À 61,5 %, il indique que moins de 62 Américains en âge de travailler sur 100 ont un emploi ou en cherchent un.

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: Pour situer le contexte, l'activité se situait à environ 63,3 % juste avant la pandémie au début de 2020, et a culminé autour de 67 % au tournant du millénaire.

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: Le long déclin depuis lors n'a rien de mystérieux dans l'ensemble : la population vieillit, et les baby-boomers qui prennent leur retraite font mécaniquement baisser le chiffre chaque année.

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: Ce qui compte pour lire le moment présent, c'est le *rythme* de la baisse et la composition de ceux qui partent.

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: Il y a une différence significative entre :

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **Sortie structurelle.** Les personnes qui partent à la retraite comme prévu, reprennent des études ou partent parce que les coûts des services de garde d'enfants et de personnes âgées dépassent ce qu'un emploi rapporte. Une croissance plus lente de la population active due à la baisse des flux migratoires apparaît également ici. Cela réduit le potentiel de l'économie au fil du temps, mais ne signale pas de faiblesse actuelle.

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **Découragement.** Les personnes qui veulent un emploi, ont cherché, n'ont rien trouvé et ont arrêté. C'est de la faiblesse cyclique déguisée — cela donne une meilleure apparence au taux de chômage précisément au moment où le marché du travail se détériore.

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: Un seul rapport mensuel ne peut pas séparer clairement les deux.

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: Les données utiles sont enfouies sous le titre : le taux d'activité des 25-54 ans (qui élimine la plupart des effets de la retraite), le nombre de personnes marginalement attachées à la population active, et la mesure plus large U-6, qui comprend les travailleurs découragés et les personnes bloquées dans des emplois à temps partiel qui veulent des heures à temps plein.

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: Si l'activité des personnes en âge de travailler glisse, la démographie de la retraite n'est pas l'explication.

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi les révisions comptent plus que d'habitude

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: Les 74 000 emplois effacés d'avril et de mai sont faciles à survoler.

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: Ils ne devraient pas l'être.

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: Les chiffres des salaires proviennent d'une enquête auprès des employeurs qui continue de recueillir des réponses pendant deux mois après la publication de la première estimation.

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: Les premiers chiffres s'appuient sur un modèle statistique qui estime les emplois créés et détruits par les entreprises trop nouvelles ou trop récemment fermées pour répondre.

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: Lorsque l'économie tourne, ce modèle a tendance à être lent — il peut surestimer la création d'emplois lorsque le cycle se refroidit et la sous-estimer lorsqu'il se réchauffe.

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: Les taux de réponse aux enquêtes ont également baissé au fil des ans, ce qui élargit la marge d'erreur pour un mois donné.

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: La conclusion pratique est qu'une série de révisions à la baisse consécutives est une information en soi.

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: Cela suggère que la première version du marché du travail a été systématiquement plus rose que la version finale — ce qui signifie que la première estimation pour juillet doit être lue en appliquant le même escompte.

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## L'argument selon lequel tout va bien

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: L'équité exige l'autre côté du bilan, et il n'est pas vide.

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: Les licenciements sont restés historiquement bas.

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: Les demandes hebdomadaires d'allocations chômage — le signal du marché du travail à plus haute fréquence disponible — n'ont pas connu de pic compatible avec un véritable ralentissement.

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: De nombreux employeurs qui ont eu du mal à recruter après 2021 semblent réticents à couper, un comportement souvent appelé thésaurisation de la main-d'œuvre.

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: Ce que cela décrit, c'est un marché à faibles embauches et faibles licenciements.

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: Si vous avez un emploi, il est assez sûr.

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: Si vous en cherchez un — un jeune diplômé, quelqu'un qui revient après une pause, quiconque essaie de changer de secteur — l'expérience est considérablement plus difficile que ne le laisse supposer un titre de 4,2%.

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: Les deux choses peuvent être vraies en même temps, et la divergence entre elles est exactement ce que le taux global obscurcit.

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: Il convient également de noter que le taux de chômage et le taux d'activité proviennent de deux enquêtes différentes.

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: Le taux et l'activité proviennent d'une enquête auprès des ménages ; le nombre d'emplois provient d'une enquête auprès des employeurs.

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: Les deux divergent régulièrement d'un mois à l'autre pour des raisons purement statistiques, et aucun n'est définitif en soi.

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## Trois points à vérifier ce vendredi

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: Le rapport de juillet tombe vendredi et offre un test direct de quelle histoire est la bonne.

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | Qu'observer | Pourquoi c'est important |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | Activité des 25-54 ans | Une hausse conjuguée à un taux stable signifie que le marché absorbe véritablement les travailleurs. Une baisse signifie que le taux est soutenu par des sorties, et non par des embauches. |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | Révisions pour mai et juin | Un quatrième mois consécutif de révisions à la baisse ferait ressembler le ralentissement à une tendance plutôt qu'à du bruit. |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | Le taux U-6 par rapport au taux principal | Un fossé qui se creuse pointe vers des travailleurs découragés et un emploi à temps partiel involontaire que le taux principal ne capture pas. |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: Si les créations d'emplois s'avèrent faibles *et* que l'activité retombe *et* que le taux se maintient près de 4,2 %, le titre est flatté par un dénominateur qui se contracte.

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: Si les créations déçoivent alors que l'activité remonte et que le taux augmente, c'est sans doute un signal plus sain — cela signifie que les gens reviennent à la recherche plutôt de l'abandonner.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## En résumé

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: Un taux de chômage stable n'est pas la même chose qu'un marché du travail stable.

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: Lorsque le bassin de personnes considérées comme recherchant un emploi ne cesse de se contracter, le taux peut rester stable, voire s'améliorer, alors que les conditions pour les demandeurs d'emploi se détériorent.

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: Rien de tout cela ne fait du 4,2 % une fabrication.

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: Cela le rend incomplet.

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: Le chiffre fait ce pour quoi il a été conçu — il n'est tout simplement pas conçu pour répondre à la question que la plupart des gens lui posent.

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: Pour quiconque suit l'économie, la bonne habitude est d'arrêter de lire le taux principal de manière isolée et de commencer à le lire comme une ligne dans une histoire à trois lignes : combien d'emplois ont été ajoutés, combien ont été retirés discrètement des mois précédents, et combien de personnes sont encore dans le décompte.

pt.title: A Ilusão de 4,2%: Por Que uma Taxa de Desemprego Estável Pode Estar Escondendo uma Força de Trabalho em Retração

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: A taxa de

segments.src: unemployment rate has become the most reassuring number in the economy — and possibly the most misleading one.
segments.tr: desemprego dos EUA tornou-se o número mais reconfortante da economia — e possivelmente o mais enganoso.

segments.src: It has been parked at 4.2%, a level that in most decades would describe a labor market in good health.
segments.tr: Ela tem permanecido em 4,2%, um nível que, na maioria das décadas, descreveria um mercado de trabalho com boa saúde.

segments.src: But the June employment report told a different story underneath the headline.
segments.tr: Mas o relatório de empregos de junho contou uma história diferente por trás da manchete.

segments.src: Payrolls grew by roughly 57,000 jobs, well short of the 115,000 economists had penciled in.
segments.tr: As folhas de pagamento cresceram em aproximadamente 57.000 empregos, bem abaixo dos 115.000 que os economistas esperavam.

segments.src: Revisions took another 74,000 jobs out of the April and May figures combined.
segments.tr: As revisões retiraram outros 74.000 empregos dos números combinados de abril e maio.

segments.src: And the labor force participation rate slipped to 61.5% — the lowest reading since March 2021, when the economy was still climbing out of the pandemic hole.
segments.tr: E a taxa de participação na força de trabalho caiu para 61,5% — o menor valor desde março de 2021, quando a economia ainda estava saindo do buraco da pandemia.

segments.src: Those three facts sit uneasily together.
segments.tr: Esses três fatos combinam-se de forma incômoda.

segments.src: Hiring slowed, past months were marked down, and yet the unemployment rate did not move.
segments.tr: A contratação desacelerou, os meses anteriores foram rebaixados e, ainda assim, a taxa de desemprego não se moveu.

segments.src: Understanding why requires looking at how the rate is built.
segments.tr: Compreender o porquê exige analisar como a taxa é construída.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## A aritmética que lisonjeia a manchete

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: A taxa de desemprego é uma fração, não uma contagem de cabeças.

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: O numerador é o número de pessoas que estão sem trabalho *e* procurando ativamente.

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: O denominador é a força de trabalho: todos os trabalhadores mais todos os que procuram ativamente.

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: Crucialmente, se você parar de procurar, você deixa ambos os lados da equação.

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: Você não é contado como desempregado.

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: Você não é contado de forma alguma.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: Um exemplo simplificado torna a mecânica óbvia.

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: Imagine uma força de trabalho de 1.000 pessoas com 42 desempregados.

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
segments.tr: A taxa é de 4,2%.

segments.src: Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: Agora suponha que 10 desses 42chem desistem de sua busca — eles se aposentam mais cedo, voltam a estudar, assumem cuidados em período integral ou simplesmente concluem que não há nada lá fora.

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: No mês seguinte, há 32 desempregados em uma força de trabalho de 990.

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: A taxa cai para aproximadamente 3,2%.

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: Ninguém encontrou um emprego.

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: O número melhorou de qualquer maneira.

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: Isso não é tanto uma falha na estatística quanto um limite no que ela foi projetada para medir.

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: A taxa de desemprego responde a uma pergunta restrita: entre as pessoas que querem trabalhar e estão procurando por isso, qual parcela não consegue encontrar?

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: Ela nunca teve a intenção de responder à pergunta mais ampla com a qual a maioria das pessoas realmente se importa — quão fácil é conseguir e manter um emprego agora?

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## O que a taxa de participação acrescenta

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: É aí que entra a taxa de participação.

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: Em 61,5%, ela diz que menos de 62 de cada 100 americanos em idade ativa estão empregados ou caçando emprego.

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: Para contexto, a participação situava-se em cerca de 63,3% pouco antes da pandemia no início de 2020, e atingiu o pico de cerca de 67% na virada do milênio.

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: O longo declínio desde então não é misterioso no agregado — a população está envelhecendo, e os baby boomers que se aposentam puxam mecanicamente o número para baixo todos os anos.

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: O que importa para ler o momento atual é o *ritmo* da queda e a composição de quem está saindo.

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: Há uma diferença significativa entre:

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **Saída estrutural.** Pessoas se aposentando conforme o cronograma, retornando aos estudos ou saindo porque os custos de cuidados infantis e de idosos excedem o que um emprego paga. O crescimento mais lento da força de trabalho devido a fluxos de imigração reduzidos também aparece aqui. Isso encolhe o potencial da economia ao longo do tempo, mas não sinaliza fraqueza atual.

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **Desencorajamento.** Pessoas que querem um emprego, procuraram, não encontraram e pararam. Esta é a fraqueza cíclica disfarçada — ela faz com que a taxa de desemprego pareça melhor justamente quando o mercado de trabalho está piorando.

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: Um único relatório mensal não consegue separar claramente os dois.

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: Os dados que ajudam estão enterrados abaixo da manchete: a taxa de participação na idade principal (25 a 54 anos, o que elimina a maioria dos efeitos de aposentadoria), a contagem de pessoas marginalmente ligadas à força de trabalho e a medida mais ampla U-6, que inclui trabalhadores desencorajados e pessoas presas em empregos de meio período que desejam horas em período integral.

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: Se a participação na idade principal estiver caindo, a demografia de aposentadoria não é a explicação.

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## Por que as revisões importam mais do que o habitual

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: Os 74.000 empregos apagados de abril e maio são fáceis de passar por cima.

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: Eles não deveriam ser.

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: Os números de folha de pagamento vêm de uma pesquisa de empregadores que continua coletando respostas por dois meses após a publicação da primeira estimativa.

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: Os números iniciais apoiam-se em um modelo estatístico que estima empregos criados e perdidos por empresas muito novas ou fechadas recentemente para responder.

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: Quando a economia muda, esse modelo tende a ser lento — ele pode superestimar a criação de empregos à medida que o ciclo esfria e subestimá-la à medida que o ciclo aquece.

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: As taxas de resposta da pesquisa também caíram ao longo dos anos, o que amplia a margem de erro em qualquer mês único.

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: A conclusão prática é que uma série de revisões consecutivas para baixo é, em si, informação.

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: Isso sugere que o primeiro rascunho do mercado de trabalho tem sido sistematicamente mais otimista do que a versão final — o que significa que a leitura inicial de julho deve ser lida com esse mesmo desconto aplicado.

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## O argumento de que as coisas estão bem

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: A justiça exige o outro lado do livro-razão, e ele não está vazio.

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: As demissões permaneceram historicamente baixas.

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: Os pedidos semanais de seguro-desemprego — o sinal de trabalho de maior frequência disponível — não dispararam de uma maneira que seria consistente com uma verdadeira recessão.

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: Muitos empregadores que lutaram para montar equipes após 2021 parecem relutantes em cortar, um comportamento frequentemente chamado de retenção de mão de obra.

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: O que isso descreve é um mercado de baixa contratação e baixa demissão.

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: Se você tem um emprego, ele é razoavelmente seguro.

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: Se você está procurando um — um recém-formado, alguém reentrando após uma pausa, qualquer pessoa tentando mudar de setor — a experiência é consideravelmente mais difícil do que uma manchete de 4,2% implica.

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: Ambas as coisas podem ser verdadeiras ao mesmo tempo, e a divergência entre elas é exatamente o que a taxa agregada obscurece.

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: Também vale a pena notar que a taxa de desemprego e a taxa de participação vêm de duas pesquisas diferentes.

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: A taxa e a participação vêm de uma pesquisa com domicílios; a contagem de folha de pagamento vem de uma pesquisa com empregadores.

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: As duas regularmente discordam de mês para mês por razões puramente estatísticas, e nenhuma é definitiva por si só.

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## Três coisas que vale a pena verificar na sexta-feira

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: O relatório de julho sai na sexta-feira e oferece um teste direto de qual história está certa.

segments.tr: | O que observar | Por que importa |

segments.tr: | Participação na idade principal (25-54) | Subir junto com uma taxa estável significa que o mercado está genuinamente absorvendo trabalhadores. Cair significa que a taxa está sendo sustentada por saídas, não por contratações. |

segments.tr: | Revisões para maio e junho | Um quarto mês consecutivo de marcas para baixo faria a desaceleração parecer uma tendência em vez de ruído. |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | A taxa U-6 versus a manchete | Um fosso que se alarga aponta para trabalhadores desencorajados e emprego involuntário de meio período que a taxa principal não captura. |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: Se as folhas de pagamento vierem fracas *e* a participação cair novamente *e* a taxa se mantiver perto de 4,2%, a manchete está sendo lisonjeada por um denominador em retração.

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: Se as folhas de pagamento decepcionarem enquanto a participação subir e a taxa subir, esse é indiscutivelmente um sinal mais saudável — significa que as pessoas estão retornando à busca em vez de abandoná-la.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## O resultado final

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: Uma taxa de desemprego estável não é a mesma coisa que um mercado de trabalho estável.

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: Quando o grupo de pessoas contadas como procurando trabalho continua encolhendo, a taxa pode se manter estável, ou até melhorar, enquanto as condições para os buscadores de emprego se deterioram.

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: Nada disso torna 4,2% uma invenção.

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: Isso a torna incompleta.

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: O número está fazendo o que foi construído para fazer — ele simplesmente não foi construído para responder à pergunta que a maioria das pessoas está fazendo a ele.

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: Para qualquer um que acompanhe a economia, o hábito útil é parar de ler a taxa principal isoladamente e começar a lê-la como uma linha em uma história de três linhas: quantos empregos foram adicionados, quantos foram retirados silenciosamente dos meses anteriores e quantas pessoas ainda estão na contagem.

in.title: Ilusi 4,2%: Mengapa Tingkat Pengangguran yang Stabil Bisa Menutupi Tenaga Kerja yang Menyusut

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengangguran

segments.src: unemployment rate has become the most reassuring number in the economy — and possibly the most misleading one.
segments.tr: AS telah menjadi angka yang paling menenangkan dalam perekonomian — dan mungkin yang paling menyesatkan.

segments.src: It has been parked at 4.2%, a level that in most decades would describe a labor market in good health.
segments.tr: Angka ini bertahan di 4,2%, level yang dalam sebagian besar dekade akan menggambarkan pasar tenaga kerja dalam kesehatan yang baik.

segments.src: But the June employment report told a different story underneath the headline.
segments.tr: Namun laporan pekerjaan bulan Juni menceritakan kisah yang berbeda di balik tajuk utama tersebut.

segments.src: Payrolls grew by roughly 57,000 jobs, well short of the 115,000 economists had penciled in.
segments.tr: Penggajian tumbuh sekitar 57.000 pekerjaan, jauh di bawah 115.000 yang diperkirakan oleh para ekonom.

segments.src: Revisions took another 74,000 jobs out of the April and May figures combined.
segments.tr: Revisi memangkas 74.000 pekerjaan lagi dari angka gabungan bulan April dan Mei.

segments.src: And the labor force participation rate slipped to 61.5% — the lowest reading since March 2021, when the economy was still climbing out of the pandemic hole.
segments.tr: Dan tingkat partisipasi angkatan kerja merosot ke 61,5% — pembacaan terendah sejak Maret 2021, ketika ekonomi masih keluar dari lubang pandemi.

segments.src: Those three facts sit uneasily together.
segments.tr: Ketiga fakta tersebut berdampingan secara tidak nyaman.

segments.src: Hiring slowed, past months were marked down, and yet the unemployment rate did not move.
segments.tr: Perekrutan melambat, bulan-bulan sebelumnya diturunkan, namun tingkat pengangguran tidak bergerak.

segments.src: Understanding why requires looking at how the rate is built.
segments.tr: Memahami alasannya memerlukan pengamatan tentang bagaimana tingkat tersebut dibangun.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline
segments.tr: ## Aritmatika yang menyenangkan tajuk utama

segments.src: The unemployment rate is a fraction, not a headcount.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengangguran adalah pecahan, bukan jumlah kepala.

segments.src: The numerator is the number of people who are out of work *and* actively looking.
segments.tr: Pembilangnya adalah jumlah orang yang tidak bekerja *dan* aktif mencari.

segments.src: The denominator is the labor force: everyone working plus everyone actively looking.
segments.tr: Penyebutnya adalah angkatan kerja: semua yang bekerja ditambah semua yang aktif mencari.

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.
segments.tr: Secara krusial, jika Anda berhenti mencari, Anda meninggalkan kedua sisi persamaan.

segments.src: You are not counted as unemployed.
segments.tr: Anda tidak dihitung sebagai pengangguran.

segments.src: You are not counted at all.
segments.tr: Anda tidak dihitung sama sekali.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.
segments.tr: Contoh yang disederhanakan membuat mekanismenya menjadi jelas.

segments.src: Imagine a labor force of 1,000 people with 42 unemployed.
segments.tr: Bayangkan angkatan kerja sebanyak 1.000 orang dengan 42 pengangguran.

segments.src: The rate is 4.2%.
segments.tr: Tingkatannya adalah 4,2%.

segments.src: Now suppose 10 of those 42 give up their search — they retire early, go back to school, take on full-time caregiving, or simply conclude that nothing is out there.
segments.tr: Sekarang misalkan 10 dari 42 orang tersebut menghentikan pencarian mereka — mereka pensiun dini, kembali ke sekolah, mengambil alih pengasuhan penuh waktu, atau sekadar menyimpulkan bahwa tidak ada apa pun di luar sana.

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: Bulan berikutnya terdapat 32 pengangguran dalam angkatan kerja sebanyak 990 orang.

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: Tingkatnya turun menjadi sekitar 3,2%.

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: Tidak ada seorang pun yang mendapatkan pekerjaan.

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: Angkanya tetap membaik.

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: Ini bukanlah kecacatan dalam statistik melainkan batas dari apa yang dirancang untuk diukur.

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: Tingkat pengangguran menjawab pertanyaan yang sempit: di antara orang-orang yang ingin bekerja dan sedang mencarinya, berapa bagian yang tidak dapat menemukannya?

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: Angka ini tidak pernah dimaksudkan untuk menjawab pertanyaan yang lebih luas yang paling dipedulikan oleh kebanyakan orang — seberapa mudahkah mendapatkan dan mempertahankan pekerjaan sekarang?

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## Apa yang ditambahkan oleh tingkat partisipasi

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: Di situlah tingkat partisipasi berperan.

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: Pada angka 61,5%, ini menyatakan bahwa kurang dari 62 dari setiap 100 orang Amerika usia kerja yang dipekerjakan atau sedang berburu pekerjaan.

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: Sebagai konteks, partisipasi berada di kisaran 63,3% tepat sebelum pandemi pada awal tahun 2020, dan mencapai puncaknya di sekitar 67% pada pergantian milenium.

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: Penurunan panjang sejak saat itu bukanlah sebuah misteri secara keseluruhan — populasi semakin tua, dan para baby boomer yang pensiun secara mekanis menarik angka tersebut turun setiap tahun.

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: Yang penting untuk membaca momen saat ini adalah *kecepatan* penurunan dan komposisi dari siapa yang pergi.

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: Ada perbedaan yang berarti antara:

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **Keluar secara struktural.** Orang-orang yang pensiun sesuai jadwal, kembali ke sekolah, atau pergi karena biaya penitipan anak dan perawatan lansia melebihi apa yang dibayarkan oleh pekerjaan. Pertumbuhan angkatan kerja yang lebih lambat dari arus imigrasi yang berkurang juga muncul di sini. Hal ini menyusutkan potensi ekonomi seiring berjalannya waktu tetapi tidak menandakan kelemahan saat ini.

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **Putus asa.** Orang yang menginginkan pekerjaan, mencari, tidak menemukan apa pun, dan berhenti. Ini adalah kelemahan siklis yang menyamar — ini membuat tingkat pengangguran terlihat lebih baik justru ketika pasar tenaga kerja memburuk.

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: Satu laporan bulanan tidak dapat memisahkan keduanya secara bersih.

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: Data yang membantu terkubur di bawah tajuk utama: tingkat partisipasi usia prima (25–54 tahun, yang menghilangkan sebagian besar efek pensiun), penghitungan orang yang terikat secara marginal dengan angkatan kerja, dan ukuran U-6 yang lebih luas, yang mencakup pekerja yang putus asa dan orang yang terjebak dalam pekerjaan paruh waktu yang menginginkan jam penuh waktu.

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: Jika partisipasi usia prima merosot, demografi pensiun bukanlah penjelasannya.

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## Mengapa revisi lebih penting dari biasanya

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: 74.000 pekerjaan yang dihapus dari bulan April dan Mei sangat mudah untuk dilewati begitu saja.

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: Seharusnya tidak demikian.

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: Angka penggajian berasal dari survei pemberi kerja yang terus mengumpulkan tanggapan selama dua bulan setelah perkiraan pertama dipublikasikan.

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: Angka-angka awal bersandar pada model statistik yang memperkirakan pekerjaan yang diciptakan dan hilang oleh bisnis yang terlalu baru atau terlalu baru tutup untuk merespons.

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: Ketika ekonomi berbalik, model tersebut cenderung lambat — model ini dapat melebih-lebihkan penciptaan lapangan kerja saat siklus mendingin dan meremehkannya saat siklus memanas.

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: Tingkat respons survei juga telah menurun selama bertahun-tahun, yang memperlebar margin kesalahan pada setiap bulan tertentu.

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: Pelajaran praktisnya adalah serangkaian revisi ke bawah secara berturut-turut adalah sebuah informasi itu sendiri.

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: Ini menunjukkan bahwa draf pertama pasar tenaga kerja secara sistematis lebih cerah daripada versi akhirnya — yang berarti cetakan awal untuk bulan Juli harus dibaca dengan diskon yang sama diterapkan.

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## Argumen bahwa semuanya baik-baik saja

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: Keadilan membutuhkan sisi lain dari buku besar, dan itu tidak kosong.

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: PHK tetap berada di level terendah secara historis.

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: Klaim mingguan untuk asuransi pengangguran — sinyal tenaga kerja frekuensi tertinggi yang tersedia — belum melonjak dengan cara yang konsisten dengan penurunan yang sebenarnya.

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: Banyak pemberi kerja yang kesulitan mengisi staf setelah tahun 2021 tampaknya enggan memangkas, sebuah perilaku yang sering disebut penimbunan tenaga kerja.

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: Apa yang digambarkan itu adalah pasar perekrutan rendah, pemecatan rendah.

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: Jika Anda memiliki pekerjaan, itu cukup aman.

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: Jika Anda sedang mencarinya — lulusan baru, seseorang yang masuk kembali setelah istirahat, siapa pun yang mencoba beralih industri — pengalamannya jauh lebih sulit daripada yang disiratkan oleh tajuk utama 4,2%.

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: Kedua hal tersebut bisa benar sekaligus, dan perbedaan di antara keduanya adalah persis apa yang dikaburkan oleh tingkat agregat.

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: Perlu juga dicatat bahwa tingkat pengangguran dan tingkat partisipasi berasal dari dua survei yang berbeda.

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: Tingkat dan partisipasi berasal dari survei rumah tangga; jumlah penggajian berasal dari survei pemberi kerja.

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: Keduanya secara teratur tidak sepakat dari bulan ke bulan karena alasan statistik murni, dan tidak ada yang definitif dengan sendirinya.

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## Tiga hal yang perlu diperiksa pada hari Jumat

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: Laporan bulan Juli dirilis pada hari Jumat dan menawarkan ujian langsung tentang cerita mana yang benar.

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | Apa yang harus dilihat | Mengapa itu penting |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | Partisipasi usia prima (25–54) | Naik seiring dengan tingkat yang stabil berarti pasar benar-benar menyerap pekerja. Turun berarti tingkat tersebut didukung oleh keluarnya pekerja, bukan perekrutan. |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | Revisi untuk Mei dan Juni | Bulan keempat berturut-turut dari angka penursunan akan membuat perlambatan terlihat seperti tren daripada kebisingan. |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | Tingkat U-6 versus tajuk utama | Kesenjangan yang melebar mengarah pada pekerja yang putus asa dan pekerjaan paruh waktu involunter yang tidak ditangkap oleh tingkat utama. |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: Jika penggajian masuk dengan lemah *dan* partisipasi turun lagi *dan* tingkatnya bertahan di dekat 4,2%, tajuk utama tersebut diuntungkan oleh penyebut yang menyusut.

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: Jika penggajian mengecewakan sementara partisipasi naik dan tingkatnya naik, itu bisa dibilang merupakan sinyal yang lebih sehat — itu berarti orang-orang kembali mencari alih-alih meninggalkannya.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Kesimpulan

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengangguran yang stabil tidak sama dengan pasar tenaga kerja yang stabil.

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: Ketika kumpulan orang yang dihitung sebagai pencari kerja terus menyusut, tingkat tersebut dapat tetap stabil, atau bahkan membaik, sementara kondisi bagi pencari kerja memburuk.

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: Tidak satupun dari ini membuat 4,2% menjadi rekayasa.

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: Ini membuatnya tidak lengkap.

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: Angka tersebut melakukan apa yang dibuat untuk dilakukannya — angka tersebut sama sekali tidak dibuat untuk menjawab pertanyaan yang diajukan oleh kebanyakan orang kepadanya.

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: Bagi siapa pun yang memantau perekonomian, kebiasaan yang berguna adalah berhenti membaca tingkat tajuk utama secara terpisah dan mulai membacanya sebagai satu baris dalam cerita tiga baris: berapa banyak pekerjaan yang ditambahkan, berapa banyak yang diam-diam diambil kembali dari bulan-bulan sebelumnya, dan berapa banyak orang yang masih ada dalam penghitungan sama sekali.

segments.src: ## The arithmetic that flatters the headline

segments.src: Critically, if you stop looking, you leave both sides of the equation.

segments.src: A simplified example makes the mechanics obvious.

segments.tr: ここで、その42人のうち10人が探索を諦めたと仮定する。彼らは早期退職するか、学校に戻るか、フルタイムの介護を引き受けるか、あるいは単に何もないと結論付けるのだ。

segments.src: The next month there are 32 unemployed in a labor force of 990.
segments.tr: 翌月には、990人の労働力の中に32人の失業者がいる。

segments.src: The rate falls to roughly 3.2%.
segments.tr: 率は約3.2%に低下する。

segments.src: Nobody found a job.
segments.tr: 誰も仕事を見つけていない。

segments.src: The number improved anyway.
segments.tr: 数字はとにかく改善した。

segments.src: This is not a flaw in the statistic so much as a limit on what it was designed to measure.
segments.tr: これは統計の欠陥というよりも、それが測定するように設計されたものの限界に近い。

segments.src: The unemployment rate answers a narrow question: among people who want work and are looking for it, what share cannot find it?
segments.tr: 失業率は、仕事を求めており探している人々のうち、何割がそれを見つけられないかという狭い質問に答えるものである。

segments.src: It was never meant to answer the broader question most people actually care about — how easy is it to get and keep a job right now?
segments.tr: それは、ほとんどの人が実際に関心を持っている、今仕事を得て維持することがどれほど簡単かというより広い質問に答えるためのものでは決してなかった。

segments.src: ## What the participation rate adds
segments.tr: ## 参加率が付け加えるもの

segments.src: That is where the participation rate comes in.
segments.tr: そこに労働参加率が登場する。

segments.src: At 61.5%, it says fewer than 62 of every 100 working-age Americans are either employed or job hunting.
segments.tr: 61.5%ということは、生産年齢のアメリカ人100人のうち62人未満しか雇用されているか仕事を探しているかのどちらでもないことを示している。

segments.src: For context, participation sat at roughly 63.3% just before the pandemic in early 2020, and peaked at around 67% at the turn of the millennium.
segments.tr: 文脈として、参加率は2020年初期のパンデミック直前には約63.3%であり、ミレニアムの転換期には約67%でピークに達した。

segments.src: The long decline since then is not mysterious in the aggregate — the population is aging, and retiring baby boomers mechanically pull the number down every year.
segments.tr: それからの長い下落は全体として謎ではない。人口は高齢化しており、退職するベビーブーマーが毎年機械的に数値を押し下げているのだ。

segments.src: What matters for reading the current moment is the *pace* of the drop and the composition of who is leaving.
segments.tr: 現在の局面を読み解く上で重要なのは、下落の*ペース*と去っていく人々の構成である。

segments.src: There is a meaningful difference between:
segments.tr: 以下の間には意味のある違いがある：

segments.src: - **Structural exit.** People retiring on schedule, returning to school, or leaving because childcare and eldercare costs exceed what a job pays. Slower labor-force growth from reduced immigration flows also shows up here. This shrinks the economy's potential over time but does not signal current weakness.
segments.tr: - **構造的離脱。** 予定通りに退職する人々、学校に戻る人々、あるいは育児や介護のコストが仕事の報酬を上回るために去る人々。移民の流れの縮小による労働力成長の鈍化もここに現れる。これは時間の経過とともに経済の潜在力を縮小させるが、現在の弱さを示唆するものではない。

segments.src: - **Discouragement.** People who want a job, searched, found nothing, and stopped. This is cyclical weakness wearing a disguise — it makes the unemployment rate look better precisely when the labor market is getting worse.
segments.tr: - **諦め（失意）。** 仕事を望み、探し、何も見つからず、やめた人々。これは変装した景気循環的な弱さであり、労働市場が悪化しているまさにその時に失業率をよく見せかける。

segments.src: A single monthly report cannot cleanly separate the two.
segments.tr: 単一の月次レポートでは、この2つをきれいに切り分けることはできない。

segments.src: The data that helps is buried below the headline: the prime-age participation rate (ages 25–54, which strips out most retirement effects), the count of people marginally attached to the labor force, and the broader U-6 measure, which includes discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time hours.
segments.tr: 役立つデータはヘッドラインの下に埋もれている：プライムエイジ参加率（25〜54歳、ほとんどの退職効果を取り除く）、労働力に周辺的にしか結びついていない人々の数、そして discouraged workers（失意の労働者）やフルタイムを望みながらパートタイムの仕事に囚われている人々を含む、より広いU-6指標である。

segments.src: If prime-age participation is sliding, retirement demographics are not the explanation.
segments.tr: プライムエイジの参加率が滑り落ちているのであれば、退職の人口統計がその説明ではない。

segments.src: ## Why the revisions matter more than usual
segments.tr: ## なぜ修正が通常より重要なのか

segments.src: The 74,000 jobs erased from April and May are easy to skim past.
segments.tr: 4月と5月から消去された7万4,000人の雇用は、サラリと読み飛ばしやすい。

segments.src: They shouldn't be.
segments.tr: そうであってはならない。

segments.src: Payroll figures come from a survey of employers that keeps collecting responses for two months after the first estimate is published.
segments.tr: 雇用統計は、最初の推計が発表された後も2ヶ月間回答を集め続ける雇用者調査から得られる。

segments.src: Early numbers lean on a statistical model that estimates jobs created and lost by businesses too new or too recently closed to respond.
segments.tr: 初期の数字は、回答するには新しすぎる、あるいは最近閉鎖されたばかりの企業によって創出および失われた雇用を推定する統計モデルに依存している。

segments.src: When the economy turns, that model tends to be slow — it can overstate job creation as the cycle cools and understate it as the cycle heats up.
segments.tr: 経済が転換するとき、そのモデルは遅くなりがちである。サイクルが冷え込むにつれて雇用創出を過大評価し、サイクルが過熱するにつれて過小評価することがある。

segments.src: Survey response rates have also drifted lower over the years, which widens the margin for error on any single month.
segments.tr: 調査の回答率も長年にわたって低下傾向にあり、それが任意の単一月における誤差の幅を広げている。

segments.src: The practical takeaway is that a run of consecutive downward revisions is itself information.
segments.tr: 実務的な教訓は、連続する下方修正の連なりそれ自体が情報であるということだ。

segments.src: It suggests the first draft of the labor market has been systematically rosier than the final version — which means the initial print for July should be read with that same discount applied.
segments.tr: それは、労働市場の初稿が最終版よりも一貫してバラ色であったことを示唆している。つまり、7月の初期値もその同じ割引を適用して読まれるべきである。

segments.src: ## The case that things are fine
segments.tr: ## 問題ないとする立場

segments.src: Fairness requires the other side of the ledger, and it is not empty.
segments.tr: 公平性を期すには台帳のもう一方の側が必要であり、それは空ではない。

segments.src: Layoffs have stayed historically low.
segments.tr: レイオフは歴史的に低い水準にとどまっている。

segments.src: Weekly claims for unemployment insurance — the highest-frequency labor signal available — have not spiked in a way that would be consistent with a genuine downturn.
segments.tr: 失業保険の週次申請件数（利用可能な最も高頻度の労働シグナル）は、本格的な景気後退と一致するような急上昇を見せていない。

segments.src: Many employers who struggled to staff up after 2021 appear reluctant to cut, a behavior often called labor hoarding.
segments.tr: 2021年以降の人員確保に苦労した多くの雇用主は削減に消極的であるように見え、この行動はしばしば労働hoarding（ホーディング／囲い込み）と呼ばれる。

segments.src: What that describes is a low-hire, low-fire market.
segments.tr: それが描写しているのは、低採用、低解雇の市場である。

segments.src: If you have a job, it is reasonably secure.
segments.tr: 仕事を持っているなら、それはかなり安全である。

segments.src: If you are looking for one — a new graduate, someone re-entering after a break, anyone trying to switch industries — the experience is considerably harder than a 4.2% headline implies.
segments.tr: 探しているなら――新卒者、ブランクからの再参入者、業界を移行しようとする人など――その経験は、4.2%のヘッドラインが意味するものよりもかなり困難である。

segments.src: Both things can be true at once, and the divergence between them is exactly what the aggregate rate obscures.
segments.tr: 両方のことが同時に真実であり得、その間の乖離こそがまさに、マクロの数値が曖昧にしているものである。

segments.src: It is also worth noting that the unemployment rate and the participation rate come from two different surveys.
segments.tr: また、失業率と参加率が2つの異なる調査から来ていることも特筆に値する。

segments.src: The rate and participation come from a survey of households; the payroll count comes from a survey of employers.
segments.tr: 失業率と参加率は家計調査から得られ、雇用者数は雇用者調査から得られる。

segments.src: The two regularly disagree month to month for purely statistical reasons, and neither is definitive on its own.
segments.tr: 純粋に統計的な理由から、この2つは毎月定期的に食い違いを見せ、どちらも単独では決定的ではない。

segments.src: ## Three things worth checking on Friday
segments.tr: ## 金曜日に確認すべき3つのこと

segments.src: The July report lands Friday and offers a direct test of which story is right.
segments.tr: 7月のレポートは金曜日に発表され、どちらの物語が正しいかを直接テストする機会を提供する。

segments.src: | What to look at | Why it matters |
segments.tr: | 見るべきポイント | なぜそれが重要か |

segments.src: | Prime-age (25–54) participation | Rising alongside a steady rate means the market is genuinely absorbing workers. Falling means the rate is being propped up by exits, not hiring. |
segments.tr: | プライムエイジ（25〜54歳）の参加率 | 安定した率と並行して上昇している場合、市場が労働者を真に吸収していることを意味する。下落している場合、採用ではなく離脱によって率が支えられていることを意味する。 |

segments.src: | Revisions to May and June | A fourth straight month of downward marks would make the slowdown look like a trend rather than noise. |
segments.tr: | 5月と6月の修正 | 4ヶ月連続の下方修正となれば、景気減速はノイズではなくトレンドのように見えるだろう。 |

segments.src: | The U-6 rate versus the headline | A widening gap points to discouraged workers and involuntary part-time employment that the main rate does not capture. |
segments.tr: | U-6率対ヘッドライン | ギャップが広がっていることは、メインの率が捉えていない失意の労働者や不本意なパートタイム雇用の存在を指し示している。 |

segments.src: If payrolls come in soft *and* participation falls again *and* the rate holds near 4.2%, the headline is being flattered by a shrinking denominator.
segments.tr: 雇用者数が軟調で*かつ*参加率が再び低下し*かつ*失業率が4.2%近辺で持ちこたえる場合、ヘッドラインは縮小する分母によって美化されていることになる。

segments.src: If payrolls disappoint while participation ticks up and the rate rises, that is arguably a healthier signal — it means people are returning to the search rather than abandoning it.
segments.tr: 雇用者数が失望させる一方で参加率が上向き、失業率が上昇する場合、それはおそらくより健全なシグナルである。つまり、人々が探索を放棄するのではなく、むしろそこに戻りつつあることを意味するからだ。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## ボトムライン（要点）

segments.src: A stable unemployment rate is not the same as a stable labor market.
segments.tr: 安定した失業率は、安定した労働市場と同じではない。

segments.src: When the pool of people counted as looking for work keeps shrinking, the rate can hold steady, or even improve, while conditions for job seekers deteriorate.
segments.tr: 仕事を探しているとカウントされるプールの縮小が続くとき、求職者にとっての条件が悪化している一方で、失業率は安定しているか、あるいは改善さえし得る。

segments.src: None of this makes 4.2% a fabrication.
segments.tr: このことのどれも、4.2%を捏造にするものではない。

segments.src: It makes it incomplete.
segments.tr: それは不完全なものにするのだ。

segments.src: The number is doing what it was built to do — it simply is not built to answer the question most people are asking of it.
segments.tr: その数字はそれが作られた通りのことをしている――単に、ほとんどの人がそれに投げかけている質問に答えるようには作られていないだけである。

segments.src: For anyone tracking the economy, the useful habit is to stop reading the headline rate in isolation and start reading it as one line in a three-line story: how many jobs were added, how many were quietly taken back from prior months, and how many people are still in the count at all.
segments.tr: 経済を追う者にとって役立つ習慣は、ヘッドラインの失業率を単独で読むのをやめ、3行の物語の1行として読み始めることである：何件の雇用が追加され、過去の月からどれだけ密かに取り戻され、どれだけの人がまだカウントの中に残っているか。

segments.tr: *この記事は一般的な情報提供のみを目的として提供されており、財務、投資、または雇用の助言を構成するものではない。

segments.tr: 引用されている雇用統計は暫定的な政府推計であり、修正の対象となる。

segments.tr: 読者は完全なデータのために米労働省労働統計局の公式発表を、個人金融に関する決定のガイダンスのために資格を持つ専門家に相談すべきである。*
